thread:
support-alex: Customer BluePeak reporting repeated 429s on their dedicated pool (dp-east-2) right after a plan change this morning. They see 429s on generation endpoints but latency otherwise looks normal. Can someone take a look?

sam-oncall: On it. Can you paste the last 200 lines from the rate-controller and the tenant quota blob? Also which pool you said? dp-east-2, got it.

support-alex: Pasting key snippets below. Logs show immediate throttles with tenant_key=f:bluepeak and quota key hit.

```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z ERROR rate-controller throttle tenant=f:bluepeak pool=dp-east-2 limit=3600/window=MINUTES used=3600
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z INFO route selection reserved_pool=quiet-pool routing=pin_to_pool
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z WARN quota-apply tenant=f:bluepeak applied=3600 denom=MINUTES source=admin-portal
```

sam-oncall: Hmm, denom=MINUTES looks suspicious. Did the plan change tool convert hours->minutes by accident?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2079 (auto-ticket, priority=P2) :rotating_light:

nidhi-sre: I pulled the quota blob from the DB: `quota:{units:3600, window:1, denom:MINUTES}` — expected for this plan should be `units:3600, denom:HOURS` (i.e., 3600 tokens/hour). With MINUTES denom that makes the effective allowed rate 60x smaller. That explains the immediate 429s.

chris-runtime: Also seeing routing sticky behavior: because the tenant is pinned to the dedicated reserved pool with burst disabled, autoscaler didn't kick in. Requests keep routing to the same noisy instance and rate-controller keeps rejecting. We need both quota rollback and to flush tenant cache so routing can rebalance.

product-liz: FYI the admin-portal change was made by @ops-admin during a support-assisted plan flip. There's a conversion helper that sometimes writes denom as MINUTES for legacy plans — I've filed a follow-up to add validation.

support-alex: Repro steps I used (from customer api key):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <bluepeak-key>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> 429 immediately
2) checked rate-controller logs and tenant quota blob
3) verified pool pinning: `GET /admin/tenant/f:bluepeak` -> `pinned_pool: dp-east-2, burst_allowed: false`

nidhi-sre: Quick remediation plan:
- rollback quota entry to correct denom (HOURS)
- flush tenant ratekey cache and prefix kv for f:bluepeak (`POST /admin/tenant/f:bluepeak/flush-rate-cache`)
- unpin from quiet pool (if pinned) or enable short burst for warmup (`PATCH /admin/tenant/f:bluepeak {"burst_allowed":true}`)

chris-runtime: Commands I'll run if you want me to exec (ops creds required):
```bash
# rollback quota
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/quotas/update \
  -d '{"tenant":"f:bluepeak","units":3600,"denom":"HOURS"}'
# flush cache
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/tenants/f:bluepeak/flush-rate-cache
```

sam-oncall: Please run the rollback + flush. I'll coordinate with BluePeak support channel and monitor. Add me if you need an emergency rollback.

support-alex: BluePeak on standby. They can tolerate a short warmup window. I'm posting ETA 15m.

ops-bot: Runbook step triggered: RB-QUOTA-01 applied by sam-oncall at 2026-03-17T09:22:00Z

nidhi-sre: Post-mortem action items proposed: validate denom on write, add a schema guard in admin-portal, and a safety check that denies denom changes that reduce effective rate by >10x without review. Also add an alert that detects sudden denom flips producing >5x drop.

chris-runtime: After rollback and flush we should see calls pass. Expect warmup delay ~30-90s due to kv cache TTL. I'll tail rate-controller and runtime logs.

sam-oncall: Rolled back quota and flushed cache at 2026-03-17T09:24:35Z. watch logs now.

support-alex: BluePeak confirms 200s now on a subset of calls, some retries needed but 429s dropped to 0. Customer happy. :thumbsup:

nidhi-sre: I'll open SRE ticket to add guard and run regression against admin-portal. tagging @product-liz

product-liz: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up on product-side validation and make sure billing/portal conversion tests cover denom semantics.

sam-oncall: Closing here, leaving INC-2026-2079 open for the SRE follow-up. If anything flares, ping me. :white_check_mark:
